thread_title: S. flava var. cuprea (ex. Bill Hoyer)
breadcrumb: S. flava var. cuprea (ex. Bill Hoyer)

posts.body_html:
Here's a S. flava var. cuprea that originally came from California Carnivores (CC's) in the 1990's. Bill Hoyer purchased this plant from CC's, and eventually, the plant was no longer in their collection. Many years later, Bill left for college and had to get rid of his collection, so the plant was given back to CC's and has stayed there ever since. This clone forms GIGANTIC specimen plants over time, and is rather impressive. The mother plant at CC's right now has more than 40+ mature pitchers on it, and each are 2+ ft tall!

Here's my puny division showing some nice colors:

posts.body_html: 'BH' on 4/16/14. Love this clone and the story behind it. I wonder where CCs got it originally? Anyway, it's busted out a pair of massive 24" pitchers to start off 2014. Great color and size - the slight ruffle to the lid is a sweet bonus too. S. flava rugelii AxB #1 is visible in the background, whereas the rather corpulent rugelli opening just behind BH is JL403.

posts.body_html:
figure I'd share some recent photos of S. flava var. cuprea "Bill Hoyer." Bill is another old school friend, and in fact, when I was 16, he went to the ICPS meeting in Georgia with me. Dude is really bright, and went to Cornell University (to study plants I think). Peter of California Carnivores always refers to him as "Billy" because that's how we remember it: as little kids, roaming around the nursery, getting our nerd on. Fortunately, there are many of you who have taken our place and will be the next generation of great Sarracenia enthusiasts who will carry on the enormous reward and responsibility of preserving these wonderful plants.

I won't bore you with anymore "old man talk"-here are the photos, which were taken 4/18/14:
